data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary package fetching a precompiled tarball from the official GitHub releases. The .install script performs typical post-install tasks (updating icon cache, notifying the user, restarting the input method daemon). While interacting with the user session from an .install script is poor packaging hygiene, it serves the package's stated purpose and is not a malicious injection. The only disagreement stems from a tool error in the Qwen report.
data.disagreement_analysis: Qwen returned 'inconclusive' because the LLM API request failed with an HTTP 400 error when auditing clak-bin.install. Deepseek successfully audited the file and correctly identified its contents as standard, albeit stylistically imperfect, post-install operations.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit clak-bin.install due to an LLM API error (HTTP 400).
learnings: The audit tool should implement retry logic or graceful degradation for transient LLM API errors (like HTTP 400) instead of failing the entire file audit and cascading to an inconclusive package verdict.

Models should be explicitly guided to distinguish between poor packaging hygiene (e.g., using sudo -u or notify-send in .install scripts to interact with user sessions) and actual malicious injections, ensuring style violations do not trigger false positive security alerts.
